agentSkillsSpec.note: The Agent Skills standard's SKILL.md keys; metadata is a map of string keys to string values. A projected SKILL.md keeps these and its harness's skillFields at the top level and carries every other key under metadata (src/adapters/copy-tree.ts, skill-frontmatter-<harness>; G22). unknownSkillFields records what the vendor page says the harness does with a key it does not define.

contracts.note: Field lists and hook events verified against current Claude Code documentation. A frontmatter key or hook event absent here is rejected by the guards, not silently tolerated.

skillFields lists the SKILL.md keys Codex documents; the projected SKILL.md keeps only those and the Agent Skills spec keys at the top level (row 131). agentFields is deliberately absent: shared agent specs are byte-identical across harnesses, so a per-harness list could only restate a subset of claude's and would change no guard outcome — an inert declaration of exactly the kind these guards exist to remove. hookEvents IS per-harness and lists the events DoFlow actually wires; widen it only with an added evidence URL.

hookEvents is empty by design, not by omission: OpenCode implements lifecycle handlers as JavaScript/TypeScript plugin modules exporting named hooks such as tool.execute.before, while DoFlow ships shell scripts invoked by a command string. The events exist natively and are recorded under capabilities.hooks.events with status "different"; wiring them would mean shipping executable code into the user's agent, which is a distribution decision rather than a projection. Widen this list only alongside that decision and an added evidence URL. See https://opencode.ai/docs/plugins.

DoFlow installs a user- or project-scope extension that registers tool_call through pi.on() and invokes the shared lifecycle bridge. Project scope requires project trust. The handler can block before tools execute; tool_execution_start remains observation-only. See https://pi.dev/docs/latest/extensions.

Copilot CLI now documents a full hook surface (use-hooks / hooks-reference, 2026): .github/hooks/*.json and ~/.copilot/hooks/, shape {version:1,hooks:{event:[entries]}} where the event name is camelCase (camelCase payload fields) or PascalCase (VS Code/Claude-compatible, snake_case payload fields). DoFlow wires none of it: the shipped scripts are Claude-payload-coupled (tool names, .session_id/.transcript_path stdin fields, CLAUDE_* envs) and Copilot's payload schemas are unverified here. hookEvents stays empty until that verification lands; widen only alongside it and an added evidence URL.

hookEvents lists only the events DoFlow actually installs a doflow.json entry for (session-context on SessionStart, pre-implementation-gate, pre-bash-guard and mcp-tool-guard all on PreToolUse — hence PreToolUse appearing once, not twice — and stop-check on Stop), not the full set of trigger names Kiro's docs confirm (SessionStart, Stop, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, UserPromptSubmit, PreTaskExec, PostTaskExec, PostFileSave, PostFileCreate, PostFileDelete, plus SessionEnd on CLI V3 only — see kiro.dev/docs/hooks/types/). Widen this list only when DoFlow wires a hook to one of the unused confirmed events, alongside an added evidence URL.

hookEvents lists what DoFlow wires; widen only with added evidence. Antigravity documents six hook events (SessionStart added); DoFlow wires PreToolUse (pre-implementation gate) and Stop (stop check) today.
